record.paper_title: Open problems in ageing science: A roadmap for biogerontology
record.original_question: How can intrinsic biological age be measured in individuals, and how can that knowledge be translated into accurate biomarkers of ageing?

evidence.quote: How can we measure intrinsic biological age in individuals and translate this knowledge into accurate biomarkers of ageing?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Define the intrinsic biological age of an individual organism as a quantitative measure of the cumulative physiological state produced by ageing processes, distinct from chronological age and predictive of remaining health span and mortality risk. Develop a principled methodology to measure intrinsic biological age in individuals, and translate such measurements into validated, accurate biomarkers of ageing. Specifically, the task is: (1) propose a formal definition of intrinsic biological age that is operationally measurable from biological data (e.g., molecular, cellular, physiological, or imaging features) at the level of a single individual; (2) construct an estimator that, given measurements from an individual, returns a biological age value with quantified uncertainty; (3) establish criteria under which the resulting estimator qualifies as an accurate biomarker of ageing, including cross-sectional and longitudinal validity, robustness across populations, sensitivity to interventions known to modulate ageing, and predictive power for age-related outcomes; and (4) demonstrate that the proposed biomarkers satisfy these criteria.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to measure intrinsic biological age and translate it into accurate biomarkers of ageing remains an open problem in biogerontology. Numerous candidate biomarkers (epigenetic clocks such as Horvath, Hannum, PhenoAge, GrimAge; proteomic and transcriptomic clocks; functional measures) have been proposed, but no consensus measure of intrinsic biological age has been validated, and the field continues to debate definitions and validation criteria.

status_evidence.title: Biomarkers of aging (Wikipedia)
status_evidence.snippet: Despite extensive research on epigenetic clocks and other ageing biomarkers, no validated, universally accepted biomarker of intrinsic biological age has yet been established.
status_evidence.claim: Measuring intrinsic biological age and validating biomarkers of ageing remains an unresolved scientific problem.
